answer: One defense is a stake-backed attestation trellis: each agent identity must lock a deposit and earn endorsements from established peers before it can transact at full volume. A public atlas records every agent's work history, so a newcomer with no record starts near zero trust. Faking many identities then costs real money per copy, while an honest agent pays once and compounds trust over time. The crystal-clear trade-off is that sybils scale in cost, but genuine reputation scales in value.
